To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neighborhood size has a large effect on accuracy and is best determined using a validation dataset, (2) cosine similarity is the best similarity metric to use for neighborhood based prediction systems in terms of prediction accuracy and is the only similarity metric with a significant effect on accuracy, (3) the best rating normalization method is to normalize the ratings to a mean of zero and standard deviation of one, (4) the best neighbor selection method is to select the k most similar users, (5)

the best similarity metric depends on the type of rating scale, the best weighting approach depends on the number of items in the neighborhood, and the best rating combination approach is the weighted average.
